doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Chicago taverns, the Vendome amateur show and his first movie
summary: Dancing for coins in a tavern at 32nd and State, an amateur show at the Vendome, and his first movie at the Lincoln Theatre; a brief question about Ruth Jones.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now I'm kind of getting ahead of myself - but there was just plenty of music around Chicago at the time in the thirties ... World's Fair; World's Fair of 1933 and World's Fair of 1934. I can remember when they opened up the taverns, Roosevelt come in and oh yes -- there was a tavern right across the street from where

we were living at the time -- 32nd and State. It would open up and one of the fellows come and got me, I guess because I was young and I could dance a little bit. We'd go in and one of them would play the piano. They had me tap dancing, they'd pass a hat, and if I made a quarter or a half dollar, I was doing good.

But I remember that period -- I'm going back -- this is 1933, just before Reverend Turner made that fiddle for me. The Vendome (phonetic) Theatre was still open, and Erskine Tate had a band in there, they used to have amateur shows -- and I wanted to get on that show so bad. I made it -- dancing. I didn't win anything cause I wasn't good enough, but the music, oh, I was crazy when I hit that stage. I don't know what routine I had; I forgot -- but the music was so beautiful.

Then another time, there was the Grand Theatre on the corner of 31st and State, and the Vendome was in the 31st block on State, and there was a little theatre called the Lincoln Theatre, and they would bring in stage shows. I remember my first movie -- of course Reverend Turner didn't know I was going. I went in, they had a stage show -- a vaudeville show -- and the movie was "City Lights" and the first talkie. Goodness, yes. The first talkie with Tom Tyler in some cowboy picture.
And I had never been to the movies; I didn't know -- nobody told me when to come out. I think I went in about 2 o'clock, and I stepped out of the show when it closed.
Was this the same time when Ruth Jones used to ask if you would go to the movies with her?
No, that was later. That was about 1936.
Yes she was, she was singing in church.
You know, but all in that neighborhood.
